name: Ryutsu-Center
tagline: Tokyo in 27 minutes and Shinagawa in 28 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥100,000 to ¥110,000.
summary: The station is in Ota City, served by Tokyo Monorail. Journey times to the main business districts are 33 minutes to Otemachi, 39 minutes to Shinjuku, 33 minutes to Shibuya and 28 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. The station stands 3.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.5 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 3.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2 m to 5.5 m, a difference of 3.5 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 3 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. For storm surge, 1 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station, OpenStreetMap records neither a clinic nor a pharmacy. The nearest hospital is いすゞ病院, about 28 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 城南福祉医療協会大田病院, about 29 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Monorail.
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Monorail. It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥100,000 to ¥110,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Showajima is ahead on lower rent and what it offers families.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Ryutsu-Center in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Ryutsu-Center. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat costs about ¥34,000 less at Showajima. On what it offers families, Showajima comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Heiwajima; for how little of the area is in the flood projection, Ryutsu-Center.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Ryutsu-Center in a straight line. Ryutsu-Center adds the Tokyo Monorail; Heiwajima adds the Keikyu Main Line. Heiwajima is at least 6 minutes quicker to Shinagawa and Roppongi. A one-room flat also costs about ¥13,000 less at Heiwajima. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, though, Ryutsu-Center comes out ahead.

notFor: People who want another route when service is suspended

noiseSources: The 首都高速1号羽田線 viaduct runs a short walk from the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
環七通り (3 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: OpenStreetMap records no supermarket within walking distance of the station.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Monorail serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
